value.body: Helps customers apply for loans — home, vehicle, personal, business or gold loans — by explaining terms, collecting documents and checking eligibility before the file goes for credit approval. Loan officers work at banks, NBFCs, housing-finance companies, microfinance institutions and loan agencies. Days mix customer meetings, document checks and follow-up on applications.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Com, BBA, BA or any graduate degree

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Loan-origination software, credit bureau reports, Excel

items.label: Key checks
items.value: KYC, income proof, credit score, property or collateral papers

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers commonly join banks, NBFCs or microfinance firms as sales officers, relationship executives or credit-processing associates through walk-ins, campus hiring or recruitment agencies. Public-sector bank posts are filled through IBPS and SBI recruitment exams, with lending duties coming later. Clear communication, comfort with numbers and local-language skills help in field roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many roles are sales-target driven, with incentives.
Growth path: loan officer → credit analyst or branch credit manager → branch manager.
RBI rules on fair lending and KYC shape the job; compliance lapses are taken seriously.
